dependency_inventory.if_down_60s: GET /ready returns 503, writes and cache-miss reads fail with 503/500; cached hot redirects continue serving if Redis is intact.
dependency_inventory.if_100x_slower: Without strict query timeouts and pool isolation, active DB connections saturate the connection pool, stalling all incoming requests including /ready and triggering upstream load balancer eviction.

dependency_inventory.if_down_60s: Cache gracefully falls back to primary DB (elevating DB read QPS); queue falls back to bounded in-memory buffer.
dependency_inventory.if_100x_slower: Every redirect blocks waiting on Redis command timeout before even attempting DB fallback, inflating P99 latency above SLA unless aggressive socket/command timeouts (<100ms) and circuit breakers trip.

dependency_inventory.if_down_60s: Immediate HTTP 5xx/ECONNREFUSED triggers async retry queue fallback without blocking API threads.
dependency_inventory.if_100x_slower: Unbounded HTTP client waits exhaust worker concurrency slots and memory, starving healthy notification channels (e.g., slow SMS provider taking down email/push delivery).

micro_exercise.down_vs_slow_conclusion: Slow is far more dangerous than down. Hard failures fail fast and free resources immediately; slow dependencies silently consume threads, sockets, memory, and connection pool slots until healthy unrelated routes collapse in a cascading outage.
